item.research_question: How does the addition of AlCoCrCuFe high entropy alloy (HEA) particles via friction stir processing affect the wear rate and coefficient of friction of copper surface composites under varying loads, sliding velocities, and sliding distances?
item.material_system: Copper matrix reinforced with AlCoCrCuFe HEA particles at 5, 10, and 15 vol%
item.processing_route: Friction Stir Processing (FSP) using a pinless tool for compaction followed by a pin tool rotating at 1000 rpm and traversing at 30 mm/min; groove dimensions: 150 mm length, 5 mm depth, and widths of 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9 mm for respective volume fractions
item.test_conditions: Pin-on-disc wear tests per ASTM G99 using a 6 mm × 6 mm × 30 mm specimen against an EN31 steel disc (65 HRC) with track radius 30 mm; variables included load, sliding velocity, and sliding distance
key_findings: Hardness of the composite reached a maximum of 149 Hv for 15% HEA reinforcement.
The base HEA reinforcement material possessed a hardness of approximately 770HV.
Wear rate decreased dramatically with HEA additions, with the minimum wear loss observed for the 15% HEA-reinforced composite.
Wear rate exhibited a positive correlation with applied load, sliding speed, and sliding distance.
Coefficient of Friction (CoF) increased with HEA addition, showing a negative correlation with wear rate.
Applied load had a severe effect on both wear rate and CoF compared to sliding velocity and sliding distance.
SEM analysis showed deep and wide grooves in unreinforced copper, while damage severity drastically reduced with HEA addition.
item.mechanism: The authors attribute improved wear resistance to the high hardness of HEA particles, fine-grain structure from FSP, and the formation of asperities where the soft matrix wears away to expose hard reinforcements that carry the load. Increased CoF is explained by the direct contact of these protruding hard reinforcements with the counterpart and the resistance of harder materials to plastic deformation.
item.limitations: The text notes that while wear resistance improves, the introduction of HEA leads to a decrement in tensile properties, and the reduction in wear rate is comparatively smaller for the 15% HEA composite compared to the 10% composite.
item.future_work: The authors state that the effect of HEA on wear resistance at different sliding conditions has not been explored in detail in previous literature, implying a need for further detailed analysis, though no specific future work is explicitly proposed in the conclusion beyond the current study's scope.
quotes: Higher hardness values at the level of 770HV were the cornerstone in its selection
The wear rate decreases dramatically with HEA additions and rises with sliding velocity, load, and sliding distance.
The incorporation of HEA to a copper matrix enhances the coefficient of friction while decreasing the wear rate.
